sources.entry: ultralytics - Ultralytics YOLO for object detection, segmentation, pose estimation, classification, and tracking.

summary.one_liner: Ultralytics YOLO, a Python package and CLI for training, running, validating and exporting YOLO models for computer vision tasks such as detection, segmentation, pose estimation, classification and tracking.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes the ultralytics package, which provides YOLO models for object detection, instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, depth estimation, image classification, pose estimation and oriented bounding boxes, with tracking of detected objects across video frames. It can be used from a yolo command-line interface or from Python via a YOLO class with train, val, predict and export methods. Export to ONNX is shown in the example. The README includes benchmark tables for YOLO26 pretrained models (n/s/m/l/x sizes) on COCO, Cityscapes, NYU Depth V2, ImageNet and DOTAv1, with CPU ONNX and T4 TensorRT speed figures. Pretrained weights download automatically on first use. Integrations with Weights & Biases, Comet ML, Roboflow and Intel OpenVINO are mentioned.
use_cases: object detection in images or video
training a custom detector on a dataset
exporting models to ONNX for deployment
how_to_run: from ultralytics import YOLO; model = YOLO("yolo26n.pt")
notable: Covers many vision tasks (detection, segmentation, semantic segmentation, depth, classification, pose, OBB) under one API
Same configuration arguments work in both CLI and Python
Published speed and accuracy tables with reproduction commands
Pretrained weights download automatically from the latest release
Dual licensing: AGPL-3.0 open source or a paid Enterprise License
caveats: Open-source use is under AGPL-3.0; commercial use without AGPL obligations requires a paid Enterprise License
YOLO27 is announced but not yet available and has no launch date
summary.license: AGPL-3.0 (open source); Ultralytics Enterprise License available for commercial use
